# What this is for

You have a run of **daily new infections** (a *window*, 30 to 365 days long, from any part of
an epidemic) and you know the population size `n`, the recovery rate `recov` and, for the SEIR
model, the incubation period `incub` (days). You want R0, the state of the epidemic on the
first day of the window (how many people are exposed, infectious and recovered), and a
prediction of the curve.

The package ships two trained **BiLSTM** calibrators, one for `epiworldR::ModelSEIRCONN` and
one for `ModelSIRCONN`, each the average of 5 networks trained on 1,000,000 simulated
epidemics. They answer in a fraction of a second, need no settings, and give an R0 range.
The package also has four standard methods set up the same way (ABC-MCMC, ABC-SMC,
differential evolution and Nelder-Mead), the scores to compare them, and the functions to
train and tune your own BiLSTM.

Only R0 = ptran x crate / recov can be learned from a curve: ptran and crate are reported but
are not separately reliable.

# 1. Calibrate a window

```{r}
library(epiworldRcalibrate)

cases <- c(12, 15, 19, 22, 30, 35, 41, 50, 61, 70, 84, 95, 110, 121, 140, 152, 170, 181, 196,
           210, 221, 230, 242, 250, 255, 260, 262, 259, 255, 250)   # daily new infections

bilstm <- window_calibrator("SEIR")
fit <- calibrate(cases, bilstm, n = 10000, recov = 1 / 7, incub = 5)
fit                        # R0 with its 95% range, ptran, crate and the starting state
calibration_estimate(fit)  # the estimates as a named vector
```

# 2. Predict the cases

`predict_cases()` turns a fit into 95% bands of the daily new infections and of the number
currently infectious, for the window and `ahead` days after it:

```{r}
band <- predict_cases(fit, ahead = 14)                       # 500 runs of the epiworldR model
band <- predict_cases(fit, ahead = 14, method = "renewal")   # the renewal equation, ~200x faster

plot(band$day, band$new_median, type = "l", ylim = range(band[, c("new_lower", "new_upper")]),
     xlab = "day", ylab = "daily new infections")
polygon(c(band$day, rev(band$day)), c(band$new_upper, rev(band$new_lower)),
        col = adjustcolor("forestgreen", 0.3), border = NA)
points(band$day, band$observed)
```

The **renewal equation** gives the model's average curve,
C_t = R0 x (S_{t-1} / n) x sum_k g_k C_{t-k}, where g is the model's generation interval
(SIR: the infectious time; SEIR: the incubation time plus the infectious time), started from
the estimated state. With `initial_state = "renewal"` the starting state (the initial cases)
is worked out by the renewal equation from the observed window instead.

# 3. Score a band

```{r}
score_band(band)            # coverage (%), band width, error of the median, interval score
interval_score(y = 25, lower = 10, upper = 30)   # 20: the width of the band
interval_score(y = 35, lower = 10, upper = 30)   # 220: the width plus 40 x the miss of 5
```

**Coverage** is the share of days inside the band. The **interval score** is the band width
plus 40 times how far a day falls outside a 95% band (Gneiting and Raftery, 2007), averaged
over the days: lower is better, and a band cannot score well just by being wide.

# 4. The standard methods

```{r}
baselines <- window_baselines("SEIR")      # ABC-MCMC, ABC-SMC, DE, Nelder-Mead
fit_de <- calibrate(cases, baselines$DE, n = 10000, recov = 1 / 7, incub = 5)
fit_de$diagnostics                        # seconds and model runs

# Other settings, for example a longer DE run:
baselines <- window_baselines("SEIR", settings = list(DE = list(itermax = 400)))
```

They search R0 (0.8 to 5) and the starting state (log10 shares) with the contact rate fixed,
and fit the curve by least squares (root mean squared error for the ABC methods), running the
epiworldR model thousands of times per window: see `?window_baselines` for their settings and
how they stop.

To search ptran and crate instead of R0:

```{r}
free <- window_baselines("SEIR", methods = "ABC-SMC", unknowns = "ptran_crate")
fit_free <- calibrate(cases, free$`ABC-SMC`, n = 10000, recov = 1 / 7, incub = 5)
fit_free$intervals          # 95% ranges of R0, ptran and crate
plot_ptran_crate(fit_free)  # the draws lie along the curve of constant R0
```

The ranges of ptran and crate are wide and that of R0 narrow: only R0 = ptran x crate / recov
shapes the curve, so ptran and crate cannot be told apart from case data.

# 5. Compare methods on many windows

```{r}
windows <- list(
  list(cases = cases, n = 10000, recov = 1 / 7, incub = 5),
  list(cases = cases[11:30], n = 10000, recov = 1 / 7, incub = 5, future = c(245, 240, 236))
)
results <- compare_methods(windows, "SEIR", cores = 4)
aggregate(cbind(coverage, interval_score, seconds) ~ method, results, mean)
plot_comparison(results)       # scores by method
plot_estimates(results, "R0")  # estimates and 95% ranges by window

# The bands of several fits side by side:
plot_bands(lapply(list(BiLSTM = fit, DE = fit_de), predict_cases, ahead = 14))
```

Add `R0`, `ptran`, `crate` (and `state`) to a window when you know the truth (simulated data)
to get the errors.

# 6. Real data

The package has daily COVID-19 cases in US states (`covid_us_states`) and Utah (`covid_utah`),
influenza and COVID-19 hospital admissions in Utah (`admissions_utah`), influenza in Baltimore
in 1918 (`flu_baltimore_1918`), and the 35 waves used in the report (`real_data_waves`).

```{r}
wave_data("Utah flu 2022-23")                           # the counts of one wave
windows <- real_data_windows("Utah flu 2022-23")        # windows from its beginning, middle and end
results <- compare_methods(windows, "SEIR", cores = 4)
```

# 7. Train and tune your own BiLSTM

For other ranges of the parameters, or another population size, simulate training data, tune
the settings and train (a GPU helps: each network took about 4 hours on a recent GPU for the
shipped SEIR model with 1,000,000 epidemics):

```{r}
data <- simulate_window_data("SEIR", n_sims = 200000, output_dir = "my_seir_data",
                             priors = list(R0 = c(0.8, 3)), cores = 16)
best <- tune_window_calibrator(data, output_dir = "my_seir_tuning", n_trials = 40)
train_window_calibrator(data, output_dir = "my_seir_model", hyperparameters = best, seeds = 1:3)

my_bilstm <- window_calibrator("SEIR", model_dir = "my_seir_model")
```
